cells.tense: You are here with the seed still open and nothing collapsed into a choice.
cells.act: let yourself want it, plainly, to yourself
cells.ask: Find the want you keep quiet. Let yourself have it plainly, with no plan attached, and tell nobody. Just carry it.
cells.core:
Something unnamed can stay unnamed around you, and it does. No verdict rushed in to make the sitting easier, no shape demanded before it's ready. That's presence, and it's rarer than it sounds. Most people push a thing to declare itself just to get out from under the waiting.

There's a want in you that hasn't been said to anyone, maybe not even to yourself. Let it be plain for once, no plan riding on it, no decision owed. Carry it like something you own. When you stop arguing with it, the direction is already there. It holds even while the route stays unclear.
cells.sheetLine: Wanting a thing plainly is not the same as deciding it.
cells.verb: holding open the seed of what has not been chosen yet
cells.place: the ground that clears when the grip loosens

cells.tense: You will keep every version open, waiting to land, and land on none.
cells.act: do one thing today the way only you do it, and do not explain it
cells.ask: Finish one small thing your way this week — imperfect, unexplained, no defense of the version you chose.
cells.core:
The options stay possible on purpose. Each one is held young so none can come out wrong, and the next version keeps looking a little more open, a little less settled, than the one you're in. It reads as care. From the far side it looks like someone who hasn't arrived, and the seed you're protecting ages where it sits.

Being what you are isn't a leap. It's one small thing done your way, done imperfectly, unexplained. No audience, no defense of the version. Landing isn't punished, and the bracing for a future you can't write stops being needed once something is actually finished.
cells.sheetLine: Keeping every version open is not the same as making one.

cells.tense: You were standing at a doorway that closed behind you, still facing it.
cells.act: look at the same thing longer, until it shows you more
cells.ask: Stay with what's already in your hands past your usual stopping point. Don't solve it. Let it show you what you missed.
cells.core:
Possibility doesn't reach you the way it once did. There's a tightness in how things get made now — the picture arrives before the work, and it arrives with hard edges. You're still making. What narrowed is the space you make things in, and the narrowing has gone quiet. Nothing here is finished, it's just held tight.

Stay with what's already in your hands past the point where you'd call it seen. Let it show you what you missed the first time. No fixing, no deciding. Knowing the tightness from inside is what starts to ease it. You may not feel different right after, and that's fine. Come back to it tomorrow.
cells.sheetLine: You're still making things, in a tighter frame than you mean to.

cells.tense: You are already in the room, and the pen has been in your hand the whole time.
cells.act: move through the fog without demanding the map
cells.ask: Take the next small step you can already see, and leave the rest of the road alone. One step is enough for now.
cells.core:
The decisions are being made by you, though you'd say the options didn't show. Ways forward shut before you caught sight of them, and the next move looks like reacting rather than picking. You hold things open without knowing your grip is what holds them. The people near you can see your hand in it better than you can.

Take the next small step you can already see. Leave the rest alone. You don't need the whole way, just enough light for this step and the one after it. The picture is already yours, and you've been calling it luck. Walking through fog without the full route is how the route gets found.
cells.sheetLine: You're picking the doors and calling the picking luck.

attempts.check: The record calls this an archetype in a house of Gestalt, and my draft treats 'Faith' as if it were folded into every card — I keep saying release in the Balanced and Too Much cells where the seat is only the place, not the medicine. Too Much and Too Little come close to swapping: both describe a person not quite in the present, one future-braced and one past-sealed, and a reader could say the Too Much cell reads as avoidance rather than hover. If the diagonal read is wrong, the person still has one real hour with what they already are, so the ask survives. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'you can hold an unnamed thing without having to name it yet,' which flatters the state instead of naming the bend.
